benchmark.costDesc: Fewer input tokens means lower API costs and more messages within your rate limit. The same quota goes further - for every AI tool you use.
benchmark.ctaDesc: Install LeanCTX and run benchmark run on your codebase. Real numbers, your files, your savings.
benchmark.demoBreakdownDesc: - tokens before and after each mode
benchmark.demoDesc: Run the benchmark on any file in your project. The output shows exact token counts for each compression mode, savings percentage, and quality preservation scores.
benchmark.demoQualityDesc: - AST, identifiers, and code lines preserved
benchmark.demoTotalsDesc: - directory-wide savings with best mode recommendation
benchmark.heroDesc: Run lean-ctx benchmark run in any project. Real token counts. Real accuracy metrics. Measured with tiktoken (o200k_base).
benchmark.metaDescription: Verify LeanCTX savings in your own codebase. Real token counts with tiktoken (o200k_base). Exact accuracy metrics for every compression mode.
benchmark.methodologyDesc: Every number on this page is reproducible. Here's exactly how we measure.
benchmark.methodTokenizerDesc: All token counts use tiktoken with the o200k_base encoding — the same tokenizer used by GPT-4o, Claude, and modern LLMs. No estimates or approximations.
benchmark.methodQualityDesc: Compressed output is only used if the composite quality score stays at or above 95%. Composite = AST preservation (50%) + identifier preservation (30%) + line coverage (20%).
benchmark.methodReproduceDesc: Run lean-ctx benchmark run src/ on your own codebase. The output shows exact token counts for each compression mode, savings percentage, and quality preservation scores.
benchmark.methodDisclaimerDesc: Results vary by file type, size, language, and read mode. The "60-99%" range reflects real-world variance: small structured files compress more, large unstructured files compress less. Cached re-reads (~13 tokens) represent the best case.
benchmark.modeDiffPreserves: Changed lines with minimal surrounding context
benchmark.modeTaskPreserves: Task-relevant code + dependency context via Knowledge Graph + IB filter
benchmark.modeFullPreserves: Everything - full content cached for re-reads at ~13 tokens
benchmark.modeMapPreserves: Code: deps + exports + signatures. Non-code: structured outlines (Markdown headings, JSON/YAML/TOML keys, lock summaries)
benchmark.modesLabel: Pick the right mode for each task
benchmark.modesSmartRead: LeanCTX's ctx_smart_read automatically picks the optimal mode using Bayesian prediction based on file type, size, and context.
benchmark.noiseDesc: Context noise dilutes the model's attention window. Removing it helps the model stay grounded in actual code structure and reduces the chance of hallucination.
benchmark.signalDesc: 10K tokens of focused context outperform 200K of boilerplate. The model spends its attention on logic, not on JSDoc comments and import boilerplate.
benchmark.stat1Desc: Compressed output is only used if the composite quality score stays at or above 95%.
benchmark.stat2Desc: Blocks low-information output with a minimum signal density of 15% (ρ).
benchmark.stat3Desc: Composite = AST 50% + identifiers 30% + lines 20% - so structure matters most.
benchmark.step1Desc: Pass a single file, a directory, or a glob pattern. The benchmark engine processes everything it finds.
benchmark.step1Title: Point at any file or directory
benchmark.step2Desc: Uses tiktoken with the o200k_base encoding (same as GPT-4o, Claude, and modern LLMs). No estimates - real token counts.
benchmark.step3Desc: Get accuracy scores and savings percentages for every compression mode. Pick the right mode for each use case.
benchmark.whyDesc1: LLMs have a fixed attention budget. Every token in the context window competes for attention weights. Filling the window with boilerplate means less attention on the code that matters.
benchmark.whyDesc2: By removing noise before it reaches the model, LeanCTX increases the information density of every request. The result: higher signal-to-noise ratio, less context dilution, and the model stays within useful context limits.
benchmark.fundDesc: Benchmark runs locally, counts tokens with the exact tokenizer, and rejects compressions that drop below the quality bar.
benchmark.fund1Desc: Counts with the same tokenizer used by modern LLMs - no estimates, no guesswork.
benchmark.fund2Desc: Scores AST preservation, identifiers, and line structure. Failing outputs are blocked automatically.
benchmark.fund3Desc: Runs on your repo. Same inputs → same numbers. Great for CI and regressions.
benchmark.beforeAfterDesc: The same file. The same information. Dramatically fewer tokens.
benchmark.modeAutoUseCase: Default - LeanCTX picks the best mode automatically
benchmark.modeAutoPreserves: Adapts per file: type, size bucket, recency, task relevance
benchmark.modeLinesUseCase: Read a specific line range - surgical precision
benchmark.modeLinesPreserves: Exact lines requested, plus minimal surrounding context
benchmark.realWorldDesc: Representative snapshots - your numbers will vary by file and codebase.
benchmark.ctaSubtext: Works on any codebase. No config needed. Results in seconds.
benchmark.advPipelineDesc: Beyond mode selection, LeanCTX applies a multi-stage optimization pipeline that adapts to file type, session context, and task intent:
benchmark.advThompsonEffect: Learns optimal compression thresholds per file type using multi-armed bandit exploration (explore vs exploit)
benchmark.advAstEffect: Language-aware pruning via Tree-sitter - removes function bodies, comments, and boilerplate while preserving API signatures
benchmark.advIdfEffect: Cross-file deduplication using inverse document frequency - eliminates content already seen in the session
benchmark.advIbEffect: Task-aware filtering using the Information Bottleneck principle - keeps only content relevant to the current task
benchmark.advVerbatimEffect: Collapses repetitive structures (imports, log lines, boilerplate) into counted summaries
benchmark.advCumulative: These stages are cumulative - applied in sequence, they can reduce a 1000-line file to under 50 tokens while preserving all task-relevant information. The pipeline is fully automatic and requires no configuration.

compatibility.mcpServerFeatureDesc: {mcpToolCount} specialized tools: ctx_read, ctx_search, ctx_graph, ctx_intent, ctx_session, ctx_task, ctx_cost, and {mcpToolMoreCount} more. Intent-aware compression, session memory, context routing, multi-agent handoffs, knowledge graphs.
compatibility.metaDescription: LeanCTX works with every AI coding tool that supports MCP. Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Windsurf, Pi, Crush, Codex, Gemini CLI, and more.
compatibility.shellHookFeatureDesc: Intercepts git, npm, cargo, docker, kubectl, pip, go, tsc, and 95+ more commands. Compresses output by 60–90%.
compatibility.shellOnlyDesc: Tools that don't support MCP still benefit from LeanCTX. The shell hook intercepts CLI commands (git, npm, cargo, docker, kubectl, ls, find, and 95+ more) and compresses their output before the AI sees it.
compatibility.standardDesc: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the open standard for connecting AI tools to external capabilities. Any future tool that supports MCP will work with LeanCTX automatically - no updates needed.

compatibility.step2Desc: Scans for Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, Windsurf, Pi, Cline, Zed, and others. Configures MCP for each.
compatibility.step3Desc: Creates the correct JSON config for each tool. No manual editing required.

docs.cliReference.knowledgeRememberDesc: Store a fact in the project knowledge base with optional confidence score.

docs.cliReference.knowledgeSearchDesc: Search across all projects and sessions for matching facts.

docs.cliReference.knowledgeImportDesc: Import facts from a JSON, JSONL, or native export file. Auto-detects input format. Default merge strategy is skip-existing (safe — never overwrites).
docs.cliReference.knowledgeRemoveDesc: Remove a specific fact from the knowledge base.
docs.cliReference.knowledgeStatusDesc: Show knowledge base summary — fact counts, categories, and last update time.
docs.cliReference.knowledgeHealthDesc: Health report with quality metrics, stale fact detection, and room balance.
docs.cliReference.sessionsMgmtDesc: Manage CCP (Context Continuity Protocol) sessions stored at ~/.lean-ctx/sessions/.
docs.cliReference.setupDesc: One-command setup. Auto-detects your shell (zsh/bash/fish/PowerShell), finds installed AI tools, and configures MCP server + shell hooks. Run once after installing LeanCTX.
docs.cliReference.setupStep2: Configures MCP for each detected AI tool
docs.cliReference.shellAliasesDesc: After running lean-ctx init --global, these aliases are available in your shell. They let you toggle compression on and off without restarting:
docs.cliReference.bypassDesc: Run any command with guaranteed zero compression. Internally sets LEAN_CTX_RAW=1 before executing the command. Use when you need absolute certainty that output is unmodified.
docs.cliReference.bypassNote: Tip: bypass is equivalent to LEAN_CTX_RAW=1 lean-ctx -c "command" but more convenient. The command string is passed directly to the shell.
docs.cliReference.initEvalNote: eval pattern: The eval method prints hook code to stdout, ensuring it always matches the installed binary version. This is the same pattern used by starship, zoxide, and atuin. Hooks are never stale after upgrades.
docs.cliReference.initStyleDesc: Controls how shell hooks are installed. By default, LeanCTX auto-detects the best approach. Users with modular dotfile managers (chezmoi, yadm, stow, oh-my-zsh) benefit from dropin style. Migration between styles is transparent — hand-edits are preserved via timestamped backups.
docs.cliReference.initStyleAuto: Auto-detect: uses drop-in if a .d/ directory exists, otherwise inline (default)
docs.cliReference.initStyleInline: Writes a fenced block directly into your shell profile (~/.zshenv, ~/.bashrc, etc.)
docs.cliReference.initStyleDropin: Creates a numbered drop-in file (e.g. ~/.zshenv.d/00-lean-ctx.zsh). Ideal for chezmoi, yadm, stow, oh-my-zsh custom/.
docs.cliReference.safetyAggressiveDesc: Heavy compression for verbose output. Still preserves error messages and safety-critical keywords.
docs.cliReference.safetyLevelsCmdDesc: Displays a detailed table showing exactly how each command type is compressed, what data is preserved, and what global safety features are active.
docs.cliReference.safetyLevelsDesc: LeanCTX categorizes every supported command into a safety level that determines how aggressively output is compressed. Higher levels never remove safety-critical information (errors, CVEs, health status).
docs.cliReference.safetyLevelsGlobalNote: Global safety features apply to ALL levels: safety-needle scan (preserves CRITICAL, FATAL, panic, CVE-*, OOMKilled, etc.), safeguard ratio (blocks >95% compression), authentication detection (masks tokens/passwords), and minimum token threshold (no compression below 50 tokens).
docs.cliReference.safetyMinimalDesc: Light formatting only. All safety-critical data (code diffs, error details, CVE IDs, health status) is fully preserved.
docs.cliReference.safetyStandardDesc: Structured compression. Errors, warnings, and actionable items always preserved.
docs.cliReference.safetyVerbatimDesc: Zero compression. Output passes through completely unmodified.
docs.cliReference.shellCompressionDesc: These commands run shell commands through LeanCTX's 95+ compression patterns. Output is automatically stripped of noise, boilerplate, and redundancy before reaching the LLM.
docs.cliReference.shellDesc: Start an interactive shell session where all command output is compressed. Wraps your default shell (zsh, bash, or fish).
docs.cliReference.slowLogDesc: Show or clear the slow command log at ~/.lean-ctx/slow-commands.log. Commands that take longer than expected are logged here for debugging.
docs.cliReference.setupPremiumNote: Since v3.3.3, the setup wizard includes a Premium Features step where you can configure Terse Agent Mode, Tool Result Archive, and Output Density interactively.
docs.cliReference.setupShellActivationNo: Since v3.5.16, setup also configures Shell Activation — you can choose when LeanCTX shell aliases auto-activate: always (default), agents-only (only when AI agent env vars are detected), or off (manual via lean-ctx-on). See Shell Activation for details.

docs.cliReference.cfgUltraCompactDesc: Enable ultra-compact output mode for maximum token savings
docs.cliReference.cfgCheckpointIntervalD: Number of MCP calls between automatic checkpoints
docs.cliReference.cfgSlowCmdThresholdDes: Threshold in milliseconds for slow-log entries
docs.cliReference.configValidateDesc: Validates config.toml against the schema. Warns about unknown keys with Levenshtein-distance "did you mean?" suggestions. Returns exit code 1 on errors (CI-friendly).
docs.cliReference.configShowDesc: Shows all effective configuration values with their source (env, config, or default). Displays simplified high-level settings and their derived downstream limits in a structured view. Useful for understanding how max_disk_mb scales memory limits proportionally.
docs.cliReference.doctorCheckLinux: Linux: systemctl --user is-active daemon state and loginctl enable-linger warning
docs.cliReference.doctorCheckCrashLoop: Crash-loop log: restart count and log file path
docs.cliReference.loginDesc: Authenticate with LeanCTX Cloud. Only attempts login - does not create a new account. If password is omitted, prompts interactively.
docs.cliReference.loginSuccessNote: On success, saves the API key to ~/.lean-ctx/cloud/credentials.json and syncs your data. If your email is not yet verified, you'll receive a reminder to check your inbox.
docs.cliReference.registerDesc: Create a new LeanCTX Cloud account. Separate from login - no auto-fallback. A verification email is sent after registration.
docs.cliReference.forgotPasswordDesc: Request a password reset email for an existing LeanCTX Cloud account.
docs.cliReference.providerDesc: Manage OAuth credentials for context providers. Currently supports Jira Cloud OAuth 2.0 (3LO) as an alternative to Basic auth (email + API token).
docs.cliReference.providerAuthNote: provider auth jira opens your browser for consent, captures the redirect on a local loopback port, discovers your accessible site (cloudId), and stores tokens in ~/.lean-ctx/credentials/jira-oauth.json (0600). Access tokens are refreshed automatically with refresh-token rotation. LeanCTX ships no embedded client secret — register your own Atlassian OAuth app and provide its credentials via env (see Configuration → Jira OAuth).
docs.cliReference.providerAuthNote2: To select OAuth for a data source, set JIRA_AUTH=oauth (or simply have a stored credential); Basic auth via JIRA_EMAIL + JIRA_API_TOKEN continues to work unchanged.
docs.cliReference.uninstallRemoves: Removes shell hooks, MCP configurations from all detected editors, .bak files, ~/.config/lean-ctx, project-local .lean-ctx/ and .lean-ctx-id, Claude CLI MCP entries, and daemon/proxy services.
docs.cliReference.uninstallKeepConfig: Use --keep-config to preserve MCP configs and rules for reinstall.
docs.cliReference.ledgerDesc: Manage the context pressure ledger. View current pressure, clear entries, evict specific files, or prune stale entries.
docs.cliReference.ledgerEvictNote: The evict action also adds exclusion overlays, preventing evicted paths from re-accumulating pressure. Use reset when switching task focus entirely.
docs.cliReference.cepInternalNote: Internally uses ctx_gain --score to compute the Context Efficiency Protocol score. The CEP score ranges from 0–100 and measures how efficiently context is being utilized across read modes, shell compression, and deduplication.
docs.cliReference.ghostDesc: Reveals hidden token waste in your workflow - shows unoptimized shell commands, redundant reads, and oversized contexts with a monthly USD savings estimate. Use --json for CI integration.
docs.cliReference.graphStatusDesc: Show graph index statistics: file count, symbol count, edge count, language breakdown, and storage path.
docs.cliReference.graphRelatedDesc: List files related to a given file based on import/dependency edges in the project graph.
docs.cliReference.graphImpactDesc: Show the blast radius — all files that depend on the given file and would be affected by changes to it.
docs.cliReference.graphSymbolDesc: Inspect a specific symbol definition. The spec format is file.rs::function_name.
docs.cliReference.graphContextDesc: Query the property graph for a concept or keyword. Searches nodes by name and returns matching definitions.
docs.cliReference.auditDesc: Generate a compliance report covering all LeanCTX activity in the current or specified project. The audit report includes file reads, compression ratios, security events, per-agent budget usage, and an OWASP alignment summary.
docs.cliReference.auditNoneDesc: Print full audit report to stdout
docs.cliReference.auditProjectDesc: Scope audit to a specific project directory
docs.cliReference.auditJsonDesc: Machine-readable JSON output for CI/CD integration
docs.cliReference.auditSectionFileReads: File Reads — total reads, unique files, cache hit rate, read modes used
docs.cliReference.auditSectionCompressio: Compression Ratios — per-mode and aggregate token savings
docs.cliReference.auditSectionSecurity: Security Events — cross-project boundary violations, blocked reads, secret detection hits
docs.cliReference.auditSectionBudget: Budget Usage — per-agent token consumption vs. configured limits
docs.cliReference.auditSectionOwasp: OWASP Alignment — summary of how LeanCTX security controls map to OWASP LLM Top 10 categories
docs.cliReference.shellAllowlistDesc: The shell_allowlist configuration restricts which commands ctx_shell can execute. When enabled, only commands matching the allowlist patterns are permitted — all others are rejected with an error. This provides an additional security layer on top of the existing safety levels.
docs.cliReference.shellAllowlistBlockedN: When a command is blocked by the allowlist, ctx_shell returns an error indicating the command is not permitted, along with the list of allowed patterns. Use lean-ctx config set shell_allowlist.enabled false to disable.
docs.cliReference.serverServicesDesc: LeanCTX can run as a long-lived HTTP server, a TUI watcher, or a network proxy. These modes are useful for CI/CD pipelines, multi-agent orchestration, and headless environments.
docs.cliReference.serveDesc: Start an HTTP/REST server that exposes all MCP tools as REST endpoints. Requires the http-server feature gate. Supports both stateful (session-persisted) and stateless modes.
docs.cliReference.serveStatelessDesc: Disable session persistence - each request is independent
docs.cliReference.serveRateLimitDesc: Max requests per minute per client
docs.cliReference.serveCorsDesc: Enable CORS headers for browser access
docs.cliReference.serveEndpointsNote: Once running, all MCP tools are available at POST /v1/tools/<tool_name>. A health endpoint is at GET /health.
docs.cliReference.watchDesc: Start LeanCTX in TUI (Terminal UI) mode with a live event bus. Monitors all MCP activity in real time and writes events to ~/.lean-ctx/events.jsonl for post-hoc analysis.
docs.cliReference.watchFilterDesc: Only show events matching the pattern (e.g. ctx_read, error)
docs.cliReference.watchNoTuiDesc: Headless mode - stream events to stdout as JSONL
docs.cliReference.proxyDesc: Manage the LeanCTX network proxy. When active, the proxy intercepts MCP traffic and applies compression transparently. Requires the proxy feature gate.
docs.cliReference.terseAgentDesc: The Terse Agent controls output density for AI agent communication. It persists across sessions and can be toggled at any time. See also the Configuration guide.

docs.cliReference.terseModeOffDesc: Terse Agent disabled - standard MCP output

docs.cliReference.terseModeUltraDesc: Maximum density: single-line responses, aggressive abbreviation, diff-only

docs.cliReference.instructionsJsonDesc: Output as JSON object with metadata
docs.cliReference.instructionsInjectDesc: Inject instructions into the active agent session
docs.cliReference.instructionsCiNote: This is particularly useful when integrating LeanCTX into CI/CD pipelines or custom agent frameworks that don't support the MCP instructions handshake natively.
docs.cliReference.lsNoGitignoreDesc: Show all files regardless of .gitignore rules. Useful for inspecting build artifacts, node_modules/, or target/ directories.
docs.cliReference.lsNote: Note: lean-ctx ls is a compressed tree view, not a drop-in ls replacement. Flags like -la, -l, -R are rejected with a clear error. Use the shell hook (ls -la directly) for standard ls behavior. By default, .gitignore rules are respected — use --no-gitignore to override.
docs.cliReference.configSchemaDesc: Outputs a complete JSON schema of all configuration keys, including types, defaults, descriptions, and env var overrides. Useful for editor autocompletion and CI validation.
docs.cliReference.dashboardProjectDesc: Scope dashboard to a specific project directory instead of the global view
docs.cliReference.packCreateDesc: Create a context package from the current project. Layers default to all available (knowledge,graph,session,patterns,gotchas).
docs.cliReference.packListDesc: List all installed packages with version and auto-load status.
docs.cliReference.packInfoDesc: Show detailed metadata, layers, stats, and integrity hash for a package.
docs.cliReference.packExportDesc: Export a package to a portable .ctxpkg file. Default output is <name>.ctxpkg.
docs.cliReference.packImportDesc: Import a package from a .ctxpkg file. Verifies SHA-256 integrity before installing.
docs.cliReference.packInstallDesc: Merge a package's context into the current project — knowledge facts, graph nodes, and gotchas.
docs.cliReference.packRemoveDesc: Remove a package from the local registry.
docs.cliReference.packAutoLoadDesc: Enable or disable auto-loading. When enabled, the package is merged into the project context automatically when ctx_overview runs at session start.
docs.cliReference.packFormatNote: The .ctxpkg format is an open file format. See the specification at ctxpkg.org
docs.cliReference.auditReportFileReads: File Reads — total reads, unique files, cache hit rate, read modes used
docs.cliReference.auditReportCompression: Compression Ratios — per-mode and aggregate token savings
docs.cliReference.auditReportSecurity: Security Events — cross-project boundary violations, blocked reads, secret detection hits
docs.cliReference.auditReportBudget: Budget Usage — per-agent token consumption vs. configured limits
docs.cliReference.auditReportOwasp: OWASP Alignment — summary of how LeanCTX security controls map to OWASP LLM Top 10 categories
docs.cliReference.terseCmdDesc: Query or set the Terse Agent mode. Without arguments, shows the current mode. With an argument, sets the mode persistently.
docs.cliReference.terseOffDesc: Terse Agent disabled - standard MCP output
docs.cliReference.terseLiteDesc: Light compression: removes boilerplate, keeps structure
docs.cliReference.terseFullDesc: Full terse mode: abbreviated keys, minimal whitespace, Fn refs
docs.cliReference.terseUltraDesc: Maximum density: single-line responses, aggressive abbreviation, diff-only
docs.cliReference.cacheMgmtDesc: Manage the LeanCTX content cache that accelerates repeated reads and avoids redundant compression.
docs.cliReference.teeDesc: Manage full output tee files saved to ~/.lean-ctx/tee/. Use lean-ctx tee last to view the most recent saved output. Configure via tee_mode: always, failures, or never.
docs.cliReference.teeManageDesc: Manage error log files stored at ~/.lean-ctx/tee/. When tee_on_error is enabled in config, failed commands log their full output here.
docs.cliReference.title: CLI Reference
docs.cliReference.packDesc: Create, manage, and share graph-native context packages using the open .ctxpkg format. Three conformance levels (Basic, Graph, Cognitive), scoped names (@scope/name), and composable knowledge graphs. LeanCTX is the reference implementation.
docs.cliReference.uninstallDesc: Remove all LeanCTX configuration: shell hooks, MCP configs from all editors, .bak files, ~/.config/lean-ctx, project-local .lean-ctx/ and .lean-ctx-id, Claude CLI MCP entries, and daemon/proxy services. Use --keep-config to preserve MCP configs for reinstall.
docs.cliReference.hardenDesc: Activate strict enforcement mode. Prevents agents from using native Read/Grep/Shell by injecting LEAN_CTX_HARDEN=1 into all discovered MCP configurations.
docs.cliReference.hardenDetails: When activated, harden mode performs the following:
docs.cliReference.hardenStep1: Sets LEAN_CTX_HARDEN=1 in all MCP server configs (Cursor, Claude, Windsurf, etc.)
docs.cliReference.hardenStep2: Optionally adds Bash to Claude Code's permissions.deny list to enforce LeanCTX shell usage
docs.cliReference.exportRulesDesc: Export high-confidence knowledge facts from the project's knowledge graph as editor-native rule files.
docs.cliReference.exportRulesNote: Only facts with confidence ≥ 0.8 and publishable archetypes (Architecture, Convention, Decision, Dependency, Gotcha) are exported. Facts carry provenance tracking.
docs.cliReference.updateDesc: Self-update the LeanCTX binary from GitHub Releases.
docs.cliReference.whenToDisable: When to disable: Turn off compression when you want to read command output yourself (debugging, reviewing logs). Turn it back on before starting an AI coding session.
docs.cliReference.wrappedDesc: Generate a shareable "Wrapped" report card of your token savings.
docs.cloud.lead: Free, opt-in cloud features for LeanCTX - sync context intelligence across devices, get adaptive compression models, and manage your knowledge graph. Just run lean-ctx login to get started. Self-hosted on LeanCTX infrastructure.
docs.cloud.loginDesc: This registers your account and links your local installation to LeanCTX Cloud.
docs.cloud.optInNote: Data contribution is opt-in. You choose during lean-ctx setup whether to share anonymized compression data.
docs.cloud.statsSyncDesc: Uploads your local compression statistics to the cloud so you can track savings across machines.
docs.cloud.title: LeanCTX Cloud
docs.cloud.yourDataIntro: We take privacy seriously. Here's exactly what we collect and what we don't:
docs.configuration.autonomyDesc: The autonomous intelligence layer runs optimization pipelines automatically.
docs.configuration.configFileDesc: LeanCTX supports an optional TOML configuration file at ~/.lean-ctx/config.toml.
docs.configuration.cursorRuleDesc1: For maximum token savings, add a .cursor/rules/lean-ctx.mdc to your project.
docs.configuration.cursorRuleDesc2: The Cursor rule includes CRP v2 (Compact Response Protocol) which can reduce both output tokens (50–80%) and thinking tokens (30–60%).
docs.configuration.description: Configuration options, environment variables, and editor setup.
docs.configuration.envActive: Recursion guard. When set, LeanCTX passes commands through without compression.
docs.configuration.envCacheTtl: Seconds of inactivity before session cache auto-clears (0 = disabled)
docs.configuration.envCheckpoint: Auto-checkpoint every N tool calls (0 = disabled)
docs.configuration.envCrpMode: Controls Token Dense Dialect compression level
docs.configuration.envDisabled: Master kill-switch. Bypasses ALL compression in both shell hook and MCP server.
docs.configuration.envRaw: Skip compression for the current command.
docs.configuration.exitCodesDesc: In shell hook mode (-c), LeanCTX forwards the exit code of the wrapped command.
docs.configuration.intro: LeanCTX works out of the box with zero configuration. All settings below are optional - defaults are tuned for typical AI-assisted development workflows.
docs.configuration.optCheckpoint: Auto-checkpoint every N tool calls (0 = disabled).
docs.configuration.optPassthrough: URL fragments for curl passthrough. Curl commands targeting these URLs skip JSON compression and return full responses.
docs.configuration.optTeeMode: When to save full output to ~/.lean-ctx/tee/. Values: always, failures, never.
docs.configuration.title: Configuration
docs.configuration.tokenCountingDesc: LeanCTX uses tiktoken-rs with the o200k_base encoding for exact token counting. No estimation, no heuristics.
docs.configuration.tomlFiltersDesc: Define custom compression rules in ~/.lean-ctx/filters/*.toml. User filters are applied before builtin patterns.
docs.configuration.tomlFiltersManage: Manage via CLI: lean-ctx filter list, lean-ctx filter validate, lean-ctx filter init (creates example).
docs.configuration.cacheEvictionDesc: The session cache uses a multi-signal eviction system: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) fuses recency, frequency, and size into a base score. On top, Hebbian co-access patterns track which files are used together, and a Boltzmann temperature mechanism adjusts eviction aggressiveness based on memory pressure. Entries with the lowest combined energy are evicted first. No manual tuning required.
docs.configuration.securityDesc: LeanCTX enforces these security boundaries automatically. No configuration needed - they are always active:
docs.configuration.pathJailDesc: All file operations are sandboxed to the project root. Symlink traversal, ../ path escapes, and absolute paths outside the project are blocked. Fixes CVE-class symlink leak vulnerabilities.
docs.configuration.shellCapDesc: Shell command output is capped at 200KB with clear truncation markers ([truncated]). Prevents memory exhaustion from runaway commands.
docs.configuration.fileSizeCapDesc: File reads are capped at 10MB. Prevents accidental ingestion of binary files or generated assets.
docs.configuration.calloutNoChangeBody: lean-ctx setup configures everything automatically. If you tune one thing, it's usually compression_level (how aggressively output is compressed) or profile. Treat the rest of this page as a reference — reach for it only when you need a specific knob.
docs.configuration.optCompressionLevelDe: Unified compression level controlling the 4-layer terse engine. "off" = no compression, "lite" = abbreviations only, "standard" = balanced compression, "max" = maximum token savings. Replaces the legacy output_density and terse_agent settings. See Compression Level.
docs.configuration.optMinimalOverheadDes: Reduce per-call token overhead to the absolute minimum. Disables auto-checkpoints, meta-strings (savings notes, stale notes, shell hints), and session/knowledge blocks in MCP instructions. Recommended for Codex, CI pipelines, and cost-sensitive environments. Also available via LEAN_CTX_MINIMAL=1. See Minimal Overhead.
docs.configuration.optOutputDensityDesc: Legacy — superseded by compression_level. Values: "normal" / "terse" / "ultra". Also available via LEAN_CTX_OUTPUT_DENSITY. See Output Density.
docs.configuration.optCustomAliasesTable: Define custom shell command aliases for ctx_shell. Each entry maps a short name to a full command. See Custom Aliases for examples.
docs.configuration.optPathJailTableDesc: Enable/disable PathJail sandbox. Set to false to allow file operations outside the project root. Useful in Docker containers or monorepos with external mounts. Also available via LEAN_CTX_NO_JAIL=1. See Security: PathJail. v3.6.7
docs.configuration.optRedirectExcludeDes: Glob patterns for files that should bypass the hook redirect and go straight to the native Read tool. Useful for config files or files you don't want compressed. Example: [".wolf/**", ".claude/**", "*.json", "CLAUDE.md"]. Also configurable via LEAN_CTX_HOOK_EXCLUDE.
docs.configuration.optContentDefinedChun: Enable Rabin-Karp content-defined chunking for ctx_read. Creates stable chunk boundaries based on content hashes, improving LLM prompt cache hit rates across edits. Opt-in: enable when working with large files that change frequently.
docs.configuration.optDisabledToolsDesc: Exclude tools from the MCP tool list to reduce token overhead. Example: ["ctx_benchmark", "ctx_metrics", "ctx_gain"]. Also available via LEAN_CTX_DISABLED_TOOLS env var (comma-separated).
docs.configuration.optTerseAgentDesc: Legacy — superseded by compression_level. Still accepted for backward compatibility ("off"/"lite"/"full"/"ultra" and true/false). If both are set, compression_level takes precedence.
docs.configuration.optRulesScopeDesc: Controls where LeanCTX injects its cursor rules. "global" = only ~/.cursor/rules/, "project" = only .cursor/rules/ in the project, "both" = both locations. See Rules Scope.
docs.configuration.optSlowCommandThresho: Commands running longer than this threshold (in milliseconds) are flagged in ctx_shell output with a timing warning. Set to 0 to disable slow command detection entirely.
docs.configuration.optBuddyEnabledDesc: Enable buddy mode for collaborative multi-agent workflows. See Buddy Mode.
docs.configuration.optExtraIgnorePattern: Additional glob patterns to exclude from ctx_tree, ctx_search, and file discovery. These are merged with the built-in ignore list (node_modules, .git, etc.). Example: ["*.generated.ts", "vendor/**", "dist/**"]
docs.configuration.optProfileDesc: Active profile name. Overridden by LEAN_CTX_PROFILE env var. Resolution order: env var → config.toml → "coder". Built-in profiles: "coder" (balanced compression), "passthrough" (full content, zero compression). Set via lean-ctx config set profile <name>.
docs.configuration.optThemeDesc: Visual theme for CLI and dashboard output.
docs.configuration.optMemoryProfileDesc: Controls memory subsystem behavior. "low" reduces memory usage at the cost of recall. "balanced" (default) optimizes for typical workflows. "performance" retains more context for maximum recall. Also available via LEAN_CTX_MEMORY_PROFILE.
docs.configuration.optBm25MaxCacheMbDesc: Maximum size in MB for the BM25 search index cache. Higher values improve search performance for large codebases.
docs.configuration.optAllowPathsDesc: Additional paths outside the project root that are allowed through the PathJail sandbox. Use for monorepo shared directories or external dependency sources.
docs.configuration.optShellHookDisabledD: Disable the shell hook entirely. When true, LeanCTX will not intercept shell commands for compression.
docs.configuration.optUpdateCheckDisable: Disable automatic version update checks. When true, LeanCTX will not check for new releases on startup.
docs.configuration.optGraphIndexMaxFiles: Maximum files scanned by the JSON graph index fallback. Increase for large monorepos. When the cap is reached, lean-ctx gain shows "(capped)" and a warning is emitted.
docs.configuration.optSandboxLevelDesc: Sandbox level for code execution. 0 = subprocess isolation only, 1 = OS-level sandboxing (Seatbelt on macOS, Landlock on Linux). Also available via LEAN_CTX_SANDBOX_LEVEL.
docs.configuration.optShellAllowlistDesc: When non-empty, only listed commands are permitted by ctx_shell. All other commands are rejected. Also available via LEAN_CTX_SHELL_ALLOWLIST (comma-separated).
docs.configuration.optNoDegradeDesc: When true, disables all automatic read mode degradation. Explicit mode=full is never downgraded by pressure or context gate. Also available via LCTX_NO_DEGRADE=1. v3.6.15
docs.configuration.optAllowAutoRerootDes: Allow automatic project root re-rooting. When false, absolute paths outside the PathJail are rejected. Also available via LEAN_CTX_ALLOW_REROOT.
docs.configuration.optAgentTokenBudgetDe: Default per-agent token budget. 0 = unlimited. Override per-agent via ctx_session.
docs.configuration.optReferenceResultsDe: When true, large tool outputs (>4000 chars) are stored as references and a URI is returned instead of the full content. Also available via LEAN_CTX_REFERENCE_RESULTS.
docs.configuration.optArchiveTableDesc: Configure zero-loss compression. Full tool results are saved to disk; the agent retrieves them on demand via ctx_expand. See Tool Result Archive.
docs.configuration.optProxyTableDesc: Upstream API proxy overrides. See Proxy.
docs.configuration.optMemoryTableDesc: Memory subsystem configuration with sub-tables for knowledge, episodic, procedural, lifecycle, gotcha, and embeddings. See Memory.
docs.configuration.optSecretDetectionTab: Regex-based secret detection in tool outputs. See Secret Detection.
docs.configuration.optBoundaryPolicyTabl: Cross-project access control and audit policy. See Boundary Policy.
docs.configuration.optBypassHintsDesc: Controls bypass detection hints when agents use native Read/Grep instead of LeanCTX tools. Values: "gentle" (reminder after cooldown), "firm" (immediate reminder), "off" (disabled). Also available via LEAN_CTX_BYPASS_HINTS.
docs.configuration.optLoopDetectionTable: Configure loop detection thresholds. See Loop Detection section below.
docs.configuration.optMemoryCleanupDesc: Controls how aggressively LeanCTX frees memory when idle. "aggressive" (default) clears caches after 5 minutes of idle time — ideal for single-IDE use. "shared" retains caches for 30 minutes — ideal when multiple IDEs or models share the same LeanCTX instance. Also available via LEAN_CTX_MEMORY_CLEANUP env var.
docs.configuration.optShellActivationDes: Controls when LeanCTX shell aliases auto-activate. "always" (default): active in every interactive shell. "agents-only": only active when AI agent env vars are detected (LEAN_CTX_AGENT, CLAUDECODE, CODEX_CLI_SESSION, GEMINI_SESSION). "off": never auto-activate, user must call lean-ctx-on manually. Also available via LEAN_CTX_SHELL_ACTIVATION env var. See Shell Activation.
docs.configuration.optMaxRamPercentDesc: Maximum percentage of system RAM that LeanCTX may use before the RAM Guardian triggers adaptive cache eviction. Range: 1–50. Also available via LEAN_CTX_MAX_RAM_PERCENT env var.
docs.configuration.optSavingsFooterDesc: Controls visibility of token savings footers (e.g. [42 tok saved (30%)]). "auto" (default): shown in CLI, suppressed in MCP/agent context. "always": always shown. "never": never shown. Also available via LEAN_CTX_SAVINGS_FOOTER env var.
docs.configuration.simplifiedConfigDesc: Instead of tuning dozens of individual limits, you can set a few high-level parameters that automatically derive downstream values. When simplified settings are used and individual limits are still at their defaults, the derived values take effect.
docs.configuration.simplifiedMaxDiskEffe: Distributes to archive.max_disk_mb (25%), bm25_max_cache_mb (10%), and proportionally scales memory limits (facts, patterns, episodes, procedures)
docs.configuration.simplifiedCompression: Sets terse agent, output density, and CRP mode in one knob
docs.configuration.simplifiedMemoryProfi: Preset for BM25 cache and runtime memory usage
docs.configuration.simplifiedConfigShowN: Use lean-ctx config show to see all effective values with their source (env / config / default / derived).
docs.configuration.envMinimalDesc: Enable minimal overhead mode. Disables auto-checkpoints, meta-strings, and session blocks in instructions. Equivalent to minimal_overhead = true in config.
docs.configuration.envNoCheckpointDesc: Disable auto-checkpoint injection without affecting other meta-strings. More targeted than LEAN_CTX_MINIMAL which disables everything.
docs.configuration.envMemoryCleanupDesc: Controls idle memory cleanup aggressiveness. aggressive: clear caches after 5 min idle (single-IDE). shared: retain caches 30 min (multi-IDE/multi-model). Overrides memory_cleanup in config.toml. If LEAN_CTX_CACHE_TTL is also set, it takes precedence for the cache TTL value.
docs.configuration.envShellActivationDes: Override shell_activation config setting. Controls when LeanCTX shell aliases auto-activate. always: active in every interactive shell. agents-only: only when AI agent env vars detected. off: manual activation via lean-ctx-on. See Shell Activation.
docs.configuration.envMaxRamPercentDesc: Maximum percentage of system RAM LeanCTX may use before the RAM Guardian triggers adaptive cache eviction. Range: 1–50. Overrides max_ram_percent in config.toml.
docs.configuration.envSavingsFooterDesc: Controls visibility of token savings footers. auto: shown in CLI, suppressed in MCP/agent context. always: always shown. never: never shown. Overrides savings_footer in config.toml.
docs.configuration.envSandboxLevelDesc: Override sandbox_level config. 0 = subprocess only, 1 = OS-level sandboxing (Seatbelt on macOS, Landlock on Linux).
docs.configuration.envShellAllowlistDesc: Override shell_allowlist config. When set, only listed commands are permitted by ctx_shell. Merges with config defaults. Example: git,cargo,npm,ls
docs.configuration.envShellAllowlistOver: Completely replaces the shell allowlist (no merging with config). Use for deterministic testing environments. Empty value ("") creates an empty allowlist (blocklist-only mode).
docs.configuration.envNoDegradeDesc: Disable all automatic read mode degradation. Explicit mode=full is never downgraded by pressure.
docs.configuration.envAllowRerootDesc: Override allow_auto_reroot config. When false (default), absolute paths outside the PathJail are rejected.
docs.configuration.envReferenceResultsDe: Override reference_results config. When true, large tool outputs (>4000 chars) are stored as references with a URI returned instead.
docs.configuration.envProfileDesc: Override active profile. Takes precedence over profile in config.toml. Built-in profiles: coder (default, balanced compression), passthrough (full content, zero compression). v3.6.19
docs.configuration.envFullToolsDesc: Register all MCP tools (including advanced/intelligence tools). Set to 0 or false to disable. Fixed in v3.6.19: =0 was previously treated as enabled
docs.configuration.envDisabledToolsDesc: Exclude specific tools from the MCP tool list. Overrides disabled_tools in config.toml when set. Example: ctx_benchmark,ctx_metrics,ctx_gain
docs.configuration.envBypassHintsDesc: Controls bypass detection hints. When agents use native Read/Grep instead of LeanCTX tools, a reminder is appended to the next response. gentle: reminder with cooldown (every 5 calls). firm: immediate reminder on every detection. off: disabled. Overrides bypass_hints in config.toml.
docs.configuration.envHardenDesc: Activate strict enforcement mode. When set, hook redirects strongly encourage LeanCTX tools by returning ALLOW JSON with embedded guidance (since v3.6.22, hooks never return DENY to avoid agent retry loops). Set automatically by lean-ctx harden.
docs.configuration.envShellDesc: Override which shell LeanCTX uses for ctx_shell / lean-ctx -c. Useful on Windows when PowerShell detection fails. Example: C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe
docs.configuration.envCompressionDesc: Override compression_level config setting. Controls the 4-layer terse engine for unified input/output compression. See Compression Level.
docs.configuration.envTerseAgentDesc: Legacy. Override terse_agent config. Mapped to compression_level internally. See Compression Level.
docs.configuration.envArchiveDesc: Override archive.enabled config. Enable zero-loss compression via the Tool Result Archive.
docs.configuration.envArchiveThresholdDe: Minimum character count before a tool result is archived. Override for archive.threshold_chars.
docs.configuration.envHeadlessDesc: Start MCP server in headless mode - skip all auto-setup (rules injection, hook installation, CLAUDE.md modification, agent registry). See Headless MCP Mode.
docs.configuration.envDataDirDesc: Override the base directory for all LeanCTX persistent data (stats, knowledge, agents, cache, sessions). All modules resolve paths through this single env var. Useful for custom data locations or containerized environments.
docs.configuration.envNoJailDesc: Disable PathJail sandbox for the current session. Useful in Docker/Podman containers or monorepos with external mounts. See PathJail Sandbox. v3.6.7
docs.configuration.envMaxReadBytesDesc: Maximum file size in bytes that ctx_read / ctx_edit will process. Files exceeding this limit are rejected with a clear error. Prevents accidental ingestion of very large files. Default: 5 MB.
docs.configuration.envMaxShellBytesDesc: Maximum shell output capture size in bytes for ctx_shell. Output exceeding this limit is truncated with a [truncated] marker. Default: 1 MB.
docs.configuration.agentModesDesc: lean-ctx init --agent <tool> supports two --agent values: hybrid (MCP reads + shell hooks, recommended) and mcp (explicit ctx_* tools only). auto selects the best default per tool (Hybrid for agents with shell access, MCP for others). A third integration mode, CLI-Redirect, removes MCP entirely and drives LeanCTX through editor rules.
docs.configuration.binaryPassthroughDesc: The hook redirect automatically detects binary files (images, PDFs, archives, fonts, videos, compiled files) by extension and passes them through to the native Read tool. This ensures AI agents can still view screenshots, images, and other non-text files without interference.
docs.configuration.autonomyEnabledDesc: Master switch. When false, all autonomy features are disabled regardless of individual settings.
docs.configuration.autonomyAutoPreloadDe: After ctx_read, automatically pre-cache files referenced via imports/includes.
docs.configuration.autonomyAutoDedupDesc: Automatically deduplicate the file cache when it exceeds dedup_threshold.
docs.configuration.autonomyAutoRelatedDe: Suggest related files based on the import graph when reading a file.
docs.configuration.autonomyAutoConsolida: Periodically consolidate knowledge base entries to merge duplicates and prune stale entries.
docs.configuration.autonomySilentPreload: Pre-cache files silently without adding output to tool responses. Disable to see which files were preloaded.
docs.configuration.autonomyDedupThreshol: Number of cached files that triggers automatic deduplication.
docs.configuration.autonomyConsolidateEv: Run knowledge consolidation every N tool calls. Higher values reduce overhead but delay cleanup.
docs.configuration.autonomyConsolidateCo: Minimum seconds between two consecutive consolidation runs, preventing rapid repeated consolidation.
docs.configuration.pathJailSandboxDesc: Every file operation is validated through a single resolve_path choke point. Paths must resolve inside the project root - symlink attacks, ../ traversal, and absolute paths outside the project are rejected. The sandbox is enforced for ctx_read, ctx_edit, ctx_search, ctx_tree, and all other file-touching tools.
docs.configuration.promptInjectionDesc: All metadata in tool responses is sanitized via neutralize_metadata - stripping control characters, encoded sequences, and injection patterns. Sensitive output blocks (knowledge, memory, gotchas) are wrapped in CSPRNG-fenced boundaries to prevent prompt injection through LLM-generated content stored in memory.
docs.configuration.toctouDesc: ctx_edit uses the same file handle for read-verify-write, preventing time-of-check-to-time-of-use race conditions where a file could be swapped between the validation and write phases.
docs.configuration.secretDetectionDesc: The [secret_detection] section configures regex-based secret detection in tool outputs. When enabled, LeanCTX scans all tool responses for patterns matching API keys, tokens, passwords, and other sensitive values.
docs.configuration.secretEnabledDesc: Enable regex-based secret detection. When enabled, tool outputs are scanned for patterns matching known secret formats (API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys).
docs.configuration.secretRedactDesc: Automatically redact detected secrets in tool output. When true, matched secrets are replaced with [REDACTED]. When false, secrets are flagged with a warning but passed through.
docs.configuration.secretCustomPatternsD: Additional regex patterns for secret detection, merged with the built-in patterns. Each entry is a regex string. Example: ["MYAPP_[A-Z0-9]{32}", "custom-secret-[a-f0-9]+"]
docs.configuration.boundaryPolicyDesc: The [boundary_policy] section controls cross-project access behavior. In monorepo or multi-project setups, this determines whether agents can search or import files across project boundaries, and whether such access is logged for audit.
docs.configuration.boundaryAllowDesc: Allow cross-project search and import. When false, file operations are restricted to the current project root. Enable for monorepo setups where agents need access across project boundaries.
docs.configuration.boundaryAuditDesc: Log cross-project access events. When true, every cross-project file access is recorded in the audit trail for compliance and security review.
docs.configuration.dataDirectoryDesc: All persistent data (stats, knowledge, agent state, sessions, cache) is stored under a single base directory, resolved in this order:
docs.configuration.cliFileCacheDesc: Since v2.21.1, lean-ctx read <file> in CLI mode caches file content to $LEAN_CTX_DATA_DIR/cli-cache/cache.json (default: ~/.lean-ctx/cli-cache/cache.json). Subsequent reads of unchanged files return a compact ~13-token cache-hit response instead of the full file content. This enables caching for CLI-mode integrations (e.g. pi-lean-ctx) that don't use the MCP server.
docs.configuration.loopDetectionDesc: LeanCTX automatically detects when an AI agent loops - calling the same or similar tools repeatedly without progress. This prevents token waste in large and monorepo projects.
docs.configuration.loopPerFingerprintDes: Tool calls are tracked using a fingerprint-based sliding window (default 5 minutes). When repeated identical calls are detected, throttling escalates:
docs.configuration.loopTriggerBlocked: Disabled by default (blocked_threshold = 0). Set to a positive value to enable.
docs.configuration.loopBehaviorBlocked: Tool call blocked with actionable guidance
docs.configuration.loopCrossToolDesc: Agents often alternate between ctx_search, ctx_shell (grep/rg/find), and ctx_semantic_search to search for the same thing. LeanCTX now tracks ALL search-related calls as a group. If more than 10 total search calls happen within the window (regardless of which tool), the agent is blocked with guidance to use ctx_tree and narrow searches with the path parameter.
docs.configuration.loopPatternDesc: Searching for "compress", then "compression", then "compress_output" is now detected as the same semantic loop. LeanCTX extracts the alpha-root of each search pattern and groups similar queries together.
docs.configuration.pipeGuardDesc: Since v2.21.6, the shell hook automatically detects when stdout is piped (not a terminal) and bypasses all compression. This prevents corruption when piping command output - for example, curl -fsSL https://example.com/install.sh | sh now works correctly even with the LeanCTX shell hook active.
docs.configuration.archiveDesc1: When compression removes details you might need later, the Tool Result Archive saves the full uncompressed output to disk and returns a reference ID. The agent can retrieve the full content at any time using ctx_expand.
docs.configuration.archiveDesc2: This is the core of zero-loss compression: the context window stays small, but no information is permanently lost.
docs.configuration.archiveStep1: A tool response exceeds the configured token threshold
docs.configuration.archiveStep2: LeanCTX stores the full output to ~/.lean-ctx/archive/ (content-addressed by SHA-256)
docs.configuration.archiveStep3: The compressed response includes an [ARCHIVE: <id>] reference
docs.configuration.archiveStep4: The agent calls ctx_expand <id> to retrieve the full content on demand
docs.configuration.archiveEnabledDesc: Enable the archive system. When disabled, compression is permanent (no retrieval).
docs.configuration.archiveThresholdChars: Minimum character count in a tool response before archiving is considered.
docs.configuration.archiveMaxAgeHoursDes: Global maximum age for archived entries. Entries older than this are purged regardless of access patterns.
docs.configuration.archiveMaxDiskMbDesc: Maximum total disk space (in MB) the archive directory may consume. Oldest entries are evicted when the limit is reached.
docs.configuration.archiveStorageDesc: Archived results are content-addressed (SHA-256 hash of the full output). Duplicate content is automatically deduplicated. Race conditions from parallel tool calls are handled via PID-unique temporary files with atomic rename.
docs.configuration.compressionLevelDesc: compression_level is the unified control for the 4-layer terse engine, replacing the legacy output_density and terse_agent settings. It governs both input compression (tool responses) and output optimization (agent responses) through a single knob.
docs.configuration.compressionOffDesc: No compression. Full tool output, no output optimization.
docs.configuration.compressionLiteDesc: Abbreviations and function references. Moderate input compression (~20-40% savings).
docs.configuration.compressionStandardDe: Balanced compression with CEP v1 protocol, delta-only output, and structured notation. Recommended when you want denser agent output.
docs.configuration.compressionMaxDesc: Maximum compression. Single-line output, aggressive truncation, symbols only. Best for CI/automated pipelines.
docs.configuration.compressionCrpDesc: compression_level and LEAN_CTX_CRP_MODE are complementary but independent. CRP mode controls the format of LeanCTX's own output (tdd/compact/off), while compression_level controls both input compression and the instructions given to the agent about how it should respond. Both can be active simultaneously for maximum token savings.
docs.configuration.compressionWhatChange: When compression is active at "standard" or above, the 4-layer terse engine applies:
docs.configuration.compressionLayer1: Layer 1: Dictionary — Common token substitutions and abbreviations
docs.configuration.compressionLayer3: Layer 3: Scoring — Information-theoretic ranking of content blocks
docs.configuration.compressionLayer4: Layer 4: Pipeline — CEP v1 protocol with delta-only output, structured notation (+/-/~), and token budgets
docs.configuration.compressionWhatChange: This can reduce total token usage by 30-50% per conversation turn. Formally verified by 82 Lean4 theorems including TerseQuality and TerseEngine proofs.
docs.configuration.terseAgentLegacyDesc: The terse_agent setting is still accepted for backward compatibility. Values are mapped automatically: "off" → Off, "lite" → Lite, "full" → Standard, "ultra" → Max. Boolean true maps to Standard.
docs.configuration.outputDensityDesc: output_density is superseded by compression_level, which unifies both input and output compression into a single setting. The legacy output_density values are still accepted and mapped automatically: "normal" → Off, "terse" → Lite, "ultra" → Max.
docs.configuration.minimalOverheadDesc: minimal_overhead reduces LeanCTX's per-call token footprint to the absolute minimum. It's designed for environments where every token counts - Codex, CI pipelines, or any cost-sensitive workflow.
docs.configuration.minNormAutoCheckpoint: Injected every N calls with session cache
docs.configuration.minWhenCodex: Codex / Claude Code CLI - these environments benefit most from reduced overhead since every token in the conversation counts against the context window
docs.configuration.minWhenCi: CI/CD pipelines - automated tasks where meta-strings add noise without value
docs.configuration.minWhenHighFreq: High-frequency tool calls - sessions with many short tool calls where per-call overhead accumulates
docs.configuration.minWhenCost: Cost optimization - when you want to minimize API costs without changing compression settings
docs.configuration.minimalImpactDesc: Combined with lazy tools (default), minimal overhead reduces per-session token overhead from ~6,600 tokens (full tools + verbose) to ~2,400 tokens (lazy + minimal) - a 64% reduction.
docs.configuration.rulesScopeDesc: Controls where LeanCTX injects its cursor rules file (lean-ctx.mdc). By default, rules are injected in both the global and project locations to ensure coverage across all Cursor workspaces.
docs.configuration.rulesGlobalUseCase: Share LeanCTX rules across all projects. Project directories stay clean.
docs.configuration.rulesProjectUseCase: Per-project rules only. Useful when global rules conflict with other tools.
docs.configuration.rulesBothUseCase: Maximum coverage - ensures LeanCTX is active regardless of how Cursor resolves rules.
docs.configuration.buddyModeDesc: Buddy mode enables collaborative multi-agent workflows. When enabled, LeanCTX coordinates context sharing between multiple agent sessions working on the same project.
docs.configuration.buddyEnabledDesc: Enable buddy mode for multi-agent collaboration. Agents can share cached files, knowledge entries, and session context via ctx_agent.
docs.configuration.customAliasesDesc: Define custom shell command aliases that expand inside ctx_shell. Useful for project-specific shortcuts that agents can use without knowing the full command.
docs.configuration.customAliasAliasDesc: The alias name. Used as ctx_shell("@test") or similar shorthand.
docs.configuration.customAliasCommandDes: The full command that the alias expands to.
docs.configuration.headlessModeDesc: By default, when LeanCTX starts as an MCP server it automatically configures the environment: injecting rules, installing hooks, updating CLAUDE.md, and registering itself. If you want full control over your configuration - for example when using a custom launcher - you can disable all auto-setup behavior.
docs.configuration.headlessWhenCustom: Custom launchers - You inject LeanCTX instructions via --append-system-prompt
docs.configuration.headlessWhenToggle: Toggle setups - You want to switch LeanCTX on/off per session
docs.configuration.headlessWhenCi: CI/CD pipelines - No interactive environment, no need for hooks
docs.configuration.headlessWhenSandbox: Sandboxed environments - You don't want LeanCTX modifying files outside the project
docs.configuration.projectIdentityDesc1: LeanCTX identifies projects by hashing their root path. In Docker or CI environments where multiple projects share the same mount path (e.g. /workspace), this can cause data collisions — graph index, semantic cache, bandit state, and embedding index from one project bleeding into another.
docs.configuration.projectIdentityDesc2: To prevent this, create a .lean-ctx-id file in your project root with a unique project name. This file takes highest priority for project identification — above git remote URL, package.json name, and directory name.
docs.configuration.projectIdentityCaches: The following data stores use a composite project hash (path + identity) to ensure isolation:
docs.configuration.projIdCacheGraph: Graph index — project dependency graph (SQLite Property Graph)
docs.configuration.projIdCacheBandit: Bandit state — multi-armed bandit model for read mode selection
docs.configuration.projIdCacheEmbedding: Embedding index — vector store for semantic search
docs.configuration.projectIdentityMigrat: When a .lean-ctx-id file is added or changed, existing data is automatically migrated from old hash directories. No manual action required.
docs.configuration.shellActivationDesc: shell_activation controls when LeanCTX shell aliases (like _lc) auto-activate in interactive shells. By default, LeanCTX activates in every shell. In team environments or CI, you may want to limit activation to AI agent sessions only.
docs.configuration.shellAlwaysBehavior: Active in every interactive shell. Default behavior, same as previous versions.
docs.configuration.shellAgentsBehavior: Only activates when AI agent environment variables are detected: LEAN_CTX_AGENT, CLAUDECODE, CODEX_CLI_SESSION, GEMINI_SESSION. Since v3.5.19, these same variables also enable tracking in non-interactive shells (e.g. Docker bash -c, Codex CLI), bypassing the TTY guard that normally disables the hook when stdout is not a terminal.
docs.configuration.shellOffBehavior: Never auto-activate. User must call lean-ctx-on manually to enable shell aliases.
docs.configuration.shellWhenAlways: always — Solo developer, want compression in every terminal
docs.configuration.shellWhenAgents: agents-only — Team environments where non-AI shells should remain unmodified. Also enables non-interactive (non-TTY) tracking for Docker/Codex containers (v3.5.19+)
docs.configuration.shellWhenOff: off — Full manual control, only enable when explicitly needed
docs.configuration.cloudDesc: The [cloud] section controls cloud integration features for LeanCTX.
docs.configuration.cloudContributeDesc: Opt-in to anonymous usage telemetry. When enabled, LeanCTX sends aggregated compression statistics to help improve the product. No code, file paths, or personal data is transmitted.
docs.configuration.providersDesc: The [providers] section controls external data sources. Provider data flows through the full consolidation pipeline — BM25, graph edges, knowledge facts, and session cache.
docs.configuration.providersEnabledDesc: Master switch for all data source providers.
docs.configuration.providersAutoIndexDes: Index provider data into BM25, Graph, and Knowledge. Set false for cache-only.
docs.configuration.providersCacheTtlDesc: TTL for in-memory provider result cache.
docs.configuration.providersMcpAuthEnvDe: Environment variable for auth token injection.
docs.configuration.jiraOauthDesc: The built-in Jira provider supports OAuth 2.0 (3-legged) as an alternative to Basic auth (JIRA_EMAIL + JIRA_API_TOKEN). LeanCTX ships no embedded client secret, so you register your own free Atlassian OAuth app at developer.atlassian.com/console/myapps (callback URL http://localhost), then export its credentials:
docs.configuration.jiraClientIdDesc: Client id of your Atlassian OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app.
docs.configuration.jiraClientSecretDesc: Client secret of the same app.
docs.configuration.jiraScopesDesc: Space-separated scopes. Default: read:jira-work read:jira-user offline_access (offline_access enables refresh tokens).
docs.configuration.jiraAuthDesc: Set to oauth to force OAuth. Otherwise OAuth is used automatically when a stored credential exists; Basic auth is the fallback.
docs.configuration.jiraTokensNote: Tokens are stored in ~/.lean-ctx/credentials/jira-oauth.json (0600) and refreshed automatically with refresh-token rotation. Manage credentials via the lean-ctx provider command.
docs.configuration.proxyDesc: The [proxy] section lets you override upstream API endpoints for LLM providers. Useful for corporate proxies, self-hosted inference, or regional routing.
docs.configuration.proxyAnthropicDesc: Custom upstream URL for Anthropic API requests. Set to your corporate proxy or self-hosted endpoint.
docs.configuration.proxyOpenaiDesc: Custom upstream URL for OpenAI API requests.
docs.configuration.proxyGeminiDesc: Custom upstream URL for Gemini API requests.
docs.configuration.memoryDesc: The [memory] section configures LeanCTX's persistent memory subsystem. Memory is organized into specialized stores — each with its own retention policy, capacity limits, and retrieval rules. Use memory_profile for a preset, or fine-tune individual sub-tables.
docs.configuration.memKnowledgeDesc: Fact store for project-level knowledge extracted from conversations and code analysis.
docs.configuration.memKnowMaxFactsDesc: Maximum number of facts stored in the knowledge base per project. Oldest entries are evicted when the limit is reached.
docs.configuration.memKnowMaxPatternsDes: Maximum number of code patterns retained.
docs.configuration.memKnowMaxHistoryDesc: Maximum history entries retained in the knowledge timeline.
docs.configuration.memKnowContradictionD: Confidence threshold for automatic contradiction detection between facts.
docs.configuration.memKnowRecallDesc: Number of facts retrieved per knowledge recall query.
docs.configuration.memKnowRoomsDesc: Maximum number of rooms returned per query.
docs.configuration.memKnowTimelineDesc: Maximum number of timeline entries returned per query.
docs.configuration.memKnowRelationsDesc: Maximum number of entity relations returned per query.
docs.configuration.memEpisodicDesc: Session-level memory capturing what happened during agent interactions.
docs.configuration.memEpiMaxEpisodesDesc: Maximum number of episodes retained across sessions.
docs.configuration.memEpiMaxActionsDesc: Maximum actions recorded per individual episode.
docs.configuration.memEpiSummaryDesc: Maximum character length for automatically generated episode summaries.
docs.configuration.memProceduralDesc: Learned procedures extracted from repeated agent workflows.
docs.configuration.memProcMaxDesc: Maximum number of learned procedures stored.
docs.configuration.memProcMinRepDesc: Minimum times a workflow pattern must repeat before it is promoted to a procedure.
docs.configuration.memProcMinSeqDesc: Minimum length of a tool-call sequence to be considered for procedure extraction.
docs.configuration.memProcMaxWindowDesc: Maximum sliding window size when scanning for repeated patterns.
docs.configuration.memLifecycleDesc: Controls how memory entries age, decay, and are pruned over time.
docs.configuration.memLifeDecayDesc: Daily decay factor applied to memory entry scores. Higher values age entries faster.
docs.configuration.memLifeLowConfDesc: Facts with confidence below this threshold are flagged as low-confidence and may be pruned earlier.
docs.configuration.memLifeStaleDesc: Number of days after which an unaccessed entry is considered stale and eligible for pruning.
docs.configuration.memLifeSimilarityDesc: Cosine similarity threshold for deduplication. Entries above this threshold are merged.
docs.configuration.memGotchaDesc: Stores project-specific gotchas — pitfalls, caveats, and non-obvious behaviors discovered during sessions.
docs.configuration.memGotchaMaxDesc: Maximum number of gotchas stored per project.
docs.configuration.memGotchaRetrievalDes: Maximum number of gotchas surfaced in a single session context.
docs.configuration.memGotchaDecayDesc: Default daily decay rate applied to gotcha importance scores. Category-specific overrides can be set via category_decay_overrides.
docs.configuration.memEmbeddingsDesc: Configuration for the vector embedding index used by semantic memory operations.
docs.configuration.memEmbMaxFactsDesc: Maximum number of facts indexed in the vector embedding store.

docs.intelligenceLayer.boltzmannIntro: Once Spectral Relevance selects the relevant files, each file needs a token budget. Naive approaches give equal budgets or sort by relevance. Boltzmann Allocation uses statistical mechanics to distribute tokens optimally.
docs.intelligenceLayer.boltzmannStep1: Each file has a relevance score Ei from Spectral Relevance.
docs.intelligenceLayer.boltzmannStep2: A temperature parameter β is derived from the task: specific tasks ("fix auth bug in login.ts") produce low temperature (sharp allocation to top files); broad tasks ("refactor the codebase") produce high temperature (even distribution).
docs.intelligenceLayer.boltzmannStep4: Minimum and maximum budgets are enforced (128–4096 tokens per file), and the compression mode (full, map, signatures) is chosen based on the allocated budget.
docs.intelligenceLayer.bpeHowItWorks: Each rule is a simple string replacement applied line-by-line after all other compression stages. Rules are derived from BPE token boundary analysis - they target patterns where the tokenizer produces unnecessarily many tokens for semantically equivalent text.
docs.intelligenceLayer.bpeImpact: BPE optimization typically saves 3–8% additional tokens on already-compressed output. The savings compound across files and are most significant for verbose languages (TypeScript, Java, C#).
docs.intelligenceLayer.bpeIntro: After all content is selected and ordered, a final pass optimizes the raw text for the LLM's BPE tokenizer. Small formatting changes can significantly reduce token count without changing semantics.
docs.intelligenceLayer.chunkingIntro: LLMs suffer from the "Lost in the Middle" problem: information at the beginning and end of context receives more attention than content in the middle. Semantic Chunking restructures output to minimize information loss.
docs.intelligenceLayer.chunkingStep1: Source lines are grouped into semantic chunks (functions, types, imports, loose logic) based on AST boundary heuristics.
docs.intelligenceLayer.chunkingStep2: Chunks matching the current task are promoted to the top (high-attention position). Remaining chunks are ordered by type priority.
docs.intelligenceLayer.chunkingStep3: Between chunks, LeanCTX inserts minimal bridge markers (---) so the LLM recognizes structural boundaries.
docs.intelligenceLayer.chunkingStep4: The last 2–3 lines of the highest-priority chunk are repeated at the very end of the output, exploiting the recency bias for critical information.
docs.intelligenceLayer.description: Six algorithms grounded in information theory, graph theory, and statistical mechanics power the context layer - filtering, prioritizing, and routing information automatically.
docs.intelligenceLayer.intro1: LeanCTX goes beyond pattern matching. Six algorithms from information theory, graph theory, and statistical mechanics work together to decide what to keep, what to cut, and where to put it - all automatically, all locally, zero configuration.
docs.intelligenceLayer.intro2: These algorithms power the autonomous intelligence layer. They activate during every ctx_read, ctx_preload, and ctx_overview call - you never invoke them directly.
docs.intelligenceLayer.mmrImpact: In a typical multi-file preload, MMR removes 10–25% of redundant content - primarily shared imports and repeated utility patterns.
docs.intelligenceLayer.mmrIntro: When multiple files are loaded into context, they often contain duplicate imports, shared boilerplate, or very similar code patterns. Maximum Marginal Relevance (MMR) removes this redundancy while preserving unique information.
docs.intelligenceLayer.mmrStep1: For each line, compute bigram Jaccard similarity against all previously selected lines (the "coverage set").
docs.intelligenceLayer.mmrStep2: The MMR score balances relevance against redundancy:
docs.intelligenceLayer.mmrStep3: Lines with MMR < 0 are suppressed - they add more redundancy than information. The λ parameter defaults to 0.7 (favoring relevance over diversity).

docs.intelligenceLayer.spectralFormula: The final relevance score combines both: 0.7 × heat + 0.3 × pagerank. Files below a threshold are excluded from preloading.
docs.intelligenceLayer.spectralGraphIntr: Two graph algorithms run on the project's dependency graph:
docs.intelligenceLayer.spectralHeatDesc: Seed files matching the task description receive initial "heat". Heat spreads along import edges with exponential decay, simulating information flow through the codebase.
docs.intelligenceLayer.spectralIntro: When you ask LeanCTX to preload context for a task, it needs to decide which files matter. Simple keyword matching only finds files that mention your search terms. Spectral Relevance finds files that are structurally connected to the relevant ones - even if they share no keywords.
docs.intelligenceLayer.spectralPageRankD: Files imported by many other files receive higher centrality scores. This identifies structural hubs (e.g., a db.ts imported by 20 modules).
docs.intelligenceLayer.spectralZeroConfi: The dependency graph builds automatically on first use via load_or_build(). No ctx_graph build needed - it just works.
docs.intelligenceLayer.surpriseImpact: Predictive Surprise removes 15–30% more boilerplate than character-level entropy while preserving complex logic. It directly models what the LLM considers "informative" because it uses the same BPE vocabulary.
docs.intelligenceLayer.surpriseIntro: Traditional compression filters use Shannon entropy on raw characters, which treats aaaa and import as equally predictable. Predictive Surprise instead measures cross-entropy against BPE token frequency - how surprising each line is to the LLM's tokenizer.
docs.intelligenceLayer.surpriseStep1: Each line is tokenized using o200k_base (GPT-4o / Claude tokenizer).
docs.intelligenceLayer.surpriseStep2: For each token, a Zipfian prior estimates expected frequency based on rank.
docs.intelligenceLayer.surpriseStep3: The cross-entropy is computed: lines with common tokens (boilerplate) score low; lines with rare tokens (complex logic) score high.
docs.intelligenceLayer.surpriseStep4: Lines below the surprise threshold are candidates for removal during aggressive compression.

docs.intelligenceLayer.verifyingDesc: Run lean-ctx benchmark run in your project to measure the combined effect of all six algorithms. The benchmark report shows per-file token savings, preservation scores (AST, identifiers, lines), and overall compression ratios.
docs.intelligenceLayer.rrfDesc: LeanCTX uses a multi-layered cache intelligence system: RRF fuses base signals (recency, frequency, size), Hebbian co-access tracking strengthens associations between co-used files, and Boltzmann temperature eviction adjusts aggressiveness based on memory pressure. A predictive prefetch model (Free Energy Principle) learns access transitions and pre-loads predicted files. A homeostatic memory guard applies graduated responses across 4 pressure levels.
docs.intelligenceLayer.rrfSignalsNew: Each signal ranked independently, then fused
docs.intelligenceLayer.rrfWeightsNew: No weights - only K=60 (standard IR parameter)
docs.intelligenceLayer.rrfEdgeLegacy: Large files dominate due to log-scaling of size
docs.intelligenceLayer.rrfEdgeNew: Fair treatment - each signal contributes equally via rank
docs.intelligenceLayer.rrfFormula: Formula: RRF(d) = Σ 1/(K + ranki(d)) - entries with the lowest fused score are evicted first. This produces monotonically correct ordering regardless of signal magnitude differences.
docs.intelligenceLayer.intentIntro: LeanCTX classifies every interaction into a StructuredIntent - a slot-based representation containing the task type, confidence, file targets, scope, language hint, urgency, and action verb. This drives all downstream decisions: which compression mode to use, how to route context, and what to prioritize.
docs.intelligenceLayer.intentTaskTypes: 9 task types are recognized: Explore, Generate, FixBug, Refactor, Test, Review, Config, Deploy, and Document. Each type triggers different compression strategies and context routing.
docs.intelligenceLayer.intentScope: IntentScope ranges from SingleFile through MultiFile and CrossModule to ProjectWide - determining how broadly context is gathered.
docs.intelligenceLayer.intentCompression: Compression adapts per intent: FixBug tasks prioritize error lines and test files via the Information Bottleneck filter, Explore tasks use lightweight cleanup to preserve structure, and Generate tasks focus on signatures and types.
docs.intelligenceLayer.intentModeSelecti: The ctx_read auto-mode selector uses the active task type to refine its decision - choosing task mode for bug fixes on large files, map mode for exploration, and signatures mode for documentation tasks.
docs.intelligenceLayer.pipelineIntro: The context pipeline processes information through six distinct layers: Input → Intent → Relevance → Compression → Translation → Delivery. Each layer has defined contracts (input/output types) and emits metrics.
docs.intelligenceLayer.pipelineMetrics: Per-layer metrics track input tokens, output tokens, compression ratio, and processing time. Aggregated across a session, these reveal where the most savings occur and which layers are bottlenecks.
docs.intelligenceLayer.ledgerIntro: The ContextLedger tracks every file sent to the AI: path, compression mode, original tokens, sent tokens, and timestamp. It calculates real-time context window utilization and pressure.
docs.intelligenceLayer.ledgerPressure: Three pressure levels: None (under 70% utilization), Compress (70–90%), and Evict (over 90%). At each level, the system takes different actions - downgrading compression modes for less relevant files or suggesting evictions.
docs.intelligenceLayer.ledgerDeficit: Context Deficit Detection identifies missing information: if a bug-fix task targets auth.rs but no test file is loaded, the system suggests tests/auth_test.rs. For config tasks, it recommends Cargo.toml, .env, or Dockerfile.
docs.intelligenceLayer.ledgerReinjection: Smart Re-Injection generates a plan to free context budget by downgrading non-target files (e.g., switching from full to signatures mode) while protecting files critical to the current intent.
docs.intelligenceLayer.multiAgentIntro: When multiple AI agents collaborate (e.g., a coder and a reviewer), LeanCTX provides structured handoffs, role-based context depth, and cross-agent knowledge sharing.
docs.intelligenceLayer.multiAgentHandoff: HandoffPackage bundles the current session ledger, structured intent, and context snapshot into a single transferable unit - so the receiving agent starts with full situational awareness instead of a blank slate.
docs.intelligenceLayer.multiAgentRoles: Seven agent roles are recognized: Coder, Reviewer, Planner, Explorer, Debugger, Tester, and Orchestrator. Each gets a tailored ContextDepthConfig - a Coder gets more full-file reads, a Reviewer gets more signatures, an Explorer gets broader graph context.
docs.intelligenceLayer.multiAgentKnowled: Cross-Agent Knowledge Sharing lets agents exchange structured facts (e.g., "discovery:auth_bug=null check missing in line 42") via a shared scratchpad. New agents inherit relevant knowledge without re-discovering it.
